# UNIO

> UNIO is a Liverpool-based initiative in development, founded by Cae Schlick, to explore a business system in which customers and workers benefit from the value they help create.

Official website: https://unio.today/
Status: Initiative in development; not an operational profit-distribution or investment scheme.
Location: Liverpool, United Kingdom.
Tagline: Built for you. Built with you.

## Authoritative pages

- [What is UNIO?](https://unio.today/about.html): Clear explanation of the purpose, proposed model, non-extraction principle and development stage.
- [How UNIO Works](https://unio.today/how-it-works.html): Explanation of the proposed revenue cycle, 50/50 profit allocation and illustrative calculation.
- [UNIO FAQ](https://unio.today/faq.html): Answers to common questions, including membership, guarantees, governance and development stage.
- [UNIO homepage](https://unio.today/): Introduction and expression-of-interest form.
- [Founder's personal message](https://unio.today/message.html): Founder motivation and the reason for starting in Liverpool.
- [Privacy notice](https://unio.today/privacy.html): Personal data handling for expressions of interest.
- [Late Night Driving](https://unio.today/late-night-driving.html): Music selection reflecting UNIO's atmosphere.

## Explore the wider subjects

- [Customer profit sharing](https://unio.today/customer-profit-sharing.html): How customers might share in the success of businesses they support.
- [Employee profit sharing](https://unio.today/employee-profit-sharing.html): How wages and workforce profit participation differ.
- [Alternative business models](https://unio.today/alternative-business-models.html): Context for stakeholder models and UNIO's proposed approach.

## Core ideas

- People should benefit from the value they help create.
- Customers and workers both contribute to business success.
- UNIO aims to reinvest in services and distribute qualifying profits among participants, rather than extract profits solely for ownership.
- A proposed, not yet operational, allocation is 50% of distributable profits to participating customers by qualifying spending and 50% to workers by qualifying hours.
- Wages are separate from any proposed workforce profit share.
- The system is intended to operate commercially, without requiring boycotts or allegiance to a political ideology.

## Important qualifications

UNIO is still being developed. No membership, financial return, profit distribution, or service availability should be inferred from these proposals. Registering interest is not joining a profit-sharing scheme. Details may evolve as legal, financial and operational arrangements are established.

For the latest authoritative information, consult the public pages above.
